title: 8 Arnold Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario

header.from: Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning

facts.label: Summary
facts.quote: This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 8 Arnold Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value according to the Statement of Significance and description of heritage attributes found in Attachment 1. The subject property at 8 Arnold Avenue is located just within the northern boundary of the Rockcliffe-Smythe neighbourhood, south of Lambton Avenue. The residence is notable as a red-brick, one-and-a-half-storey, Ontario Farmhouse-style property, dating from c.1870s – 1880s, and historically known as the George Marshall Residence. The property, which is the earliest known house in the Mount Dennis community, serves to recall the community’s former farming and settlement past. A location map and current photograph of the property are found in Attachment 2. In 2021 the Mount Dennis Cultural Heritage Resource Assessment (CHRA) was completed by the heritage consulting firm, Common Bond Collective, as part of the Picture Mount Dennis Planning Framework Study. The CHRA identified the property at 8 Arnold Avenue as having potential heritage value for its design/physical, and historical/associative value. The Mount Dennis Secondary Plan and the associated Official Plan Amendment (OPA 571) was approved by the Ontario Land Tribunal on October 11, 2024. City Council listed the property at 8 Arnold Avenue on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on May 20, 2026. On August 19, 2026, Toronto Building received an application to demolish the dwelling at 8 Arnold Avenue. On October 14, 2026, Toronto Building issued an Applicable Law Notice to the applicant identifying outstanding requirements relating to demolition control under S.33 of the Planning Act and notice under the Ontario Heritage Act. 8 Arnold Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate Page 1 of 19 The owner must submit to Heritage Planning a Notice of Intention to Demolish, as required under S.27(9) of the Ontario Heritage Act, to give a municipal council at least 60 days’ notice in writing of their intention to demolish or remove a structure on a “listed” property. This allows Council time to decide whether to move forward with a notice of intention to designate the property under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act. At the time of this report, the owner had not yet submitted the notice to Heritage Planning. Staff have determined that the property at 8 Arnold Avenue has cultural heritage value and meets three of the Ontario Regulation 9/06 criteria prescribed for municipal designation under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. A property may be designated under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, if it meets two or more of the nine criteria. Designation enables City Council to review proposed alterations or demolitions to the property and enforce heritage property standards and maintenance.

facts.label: Recommendations
facts.quote: The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that: 1. City Council state its intention to designate the property at 8 Arnold Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 8 Arnold Avenue (Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the report, October 28, 2026, from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning. 2. If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.

facts.label: Financial impact
facts.quote: There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer has reviewed this report and agrees with the information as presented in the Financial Impact Section.

facts.label: Decision history
facts.quote: City Council listed the property at 8 Arnold Avenue on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on May 20, 2026 https://secure.toronto.ca/council/agenda-item.do?item=2026.CC41.17 8 Arnold Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate Page 2 of 19 City Council adopted the Mount Dennis Secondary Plan on July 19, 20, 21, 2022 https://secure.toronto.ca/council/agenda-item.do?item=2022.EY33.11 POLICY AND REGULATION CONSIDERATIONS Provincial Plans and Policies The conservation of cultural heritage resources is an integral component of good planning, contributing to a sense of place, economic prosperity, and healthy and equitable communities. Heritage conservation in Ontario is identified as a provincial interest under the Planning Act. https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90p13 Further, the policies and definitions of the Provincial Planning Statement (2024) identify the Ontario Heritage Act as the primary legislation through which heritage evaluation and heritage conservation will be implemented. https://www.ontario.ca/files/2024-08/mmah-provincial-planning-statement-en-2024-08- 19.pdf Ontario Regulation 9/06 sets out the criteria for evaluating properties to be designated under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The criteria are based on an evaluation of design/physical value, historical and associative value and contextual value. A property may be designated under Section 29 of the Act if it meets two or more of the provincial criteria for determining whether it is of cultural heritage value or interest. https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/060009 Official Plan The City of Toronto's Official Plan implements the provincial policy regime and provides policies to guide decision making within the City. It contains a number of policies related to properties on the City’s Heritage Register and properties adjacent to them, as well as the protection of areas of archaeological potential. The Official Plan should be read as a whole to understand its comprehensive and integrative intent as a policy framework for priority setting and decision making. The Official Plan can be found here: https://www.toronto.ca/city-government/planning-development/official-plan- guidelines/official-plan/
